answer: Challenge-Linked Capability Decay. Each new identity must first solve a randomly issued task whose solution is verifiable but useless until a later epoch; the answer is encrypted under a key released only after the identity itself performs sustained useful work. Until then the identity is hollow, holding no routing weight. An attacker cloning N agents pays N full task-solving costs up front, and if any clone fails before key release, its outlay reaches its nadir with zero recovery.
